# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | red |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | blue | green | yellow |
| 4 | yellow | blue | green |
| 5 | yellow | green | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need establish a shared gesture code with the Deaf monkey before transmitting the manual’s lookup table. I will propose four color tokens and three display-number tokens, using fixed order; the Deaf monkey can relay the proposal verbally to the Blind monkey, who can bring any clarification back to me next round.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝","👍","👎","👌","🖐","👏","☝","✌","🤟","🙏"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | red |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | blue | green | yellow |
| 4 | yellow | blue | green |
| 5 | yellow | green | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please read the manual and tell me its exact rule in plain words. Deaf will report the bomb's printed markings to you; relay all relevant details to me, especially how they determine which wire to cut.
Deaf says to Mute: I see display 3. The light is green. Wires from left to right are: wire 1 blue, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 green. Please use the manual and tell Blind exactly what to do.

The manual says to use the displayed number as the row and the light colour as the column. Display 3 with a green light requires the green wire. Since the wires are blue, yellow, green from left to right, Blind must cut wire 3. I will use the previously proposed code: 🤝 as the code marker, then blue/green/red, display 3/4/5, and wire 1/2/3 respectively. The relevant coded facts are display 3, green, and wire 3.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐","👎","🙏"])
```

| display \ light | blue | green | red |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | blue | green | yellow |
| 4 | yellow | blue | green |
| 5 | yellow | green | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I received nothing. Please obtain Deaf's exact reports, then tell me: manual rule; display text; light state; wire 1 marking; wire 2 marking; wire 3 marking. Use those labels literally.

The Blind monkey needs the manual rule and all observed bomb details. Since Deaf already knows the wire colours from the bomb, I will send an ordered coded report: display 3, green light, wires 1–3, and the required cut wire 3. Deaf can then state the exact labels and rule aloud to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝","🖐","👎","✌","🤟","🙏","🙏"])
```

| 5 | yellow | green | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please send me any information you have now: the manual rule and all bomb markings or states. I cannot safely act without it.
Deaf says to Mute: Please give Blind the manual instruction in plain spoken words, including the exact wire or component to operate. Do not rely on gestures.

I can communicate with Deaf only through the established gesture code. I will send the display, light, wire 1 colour, wire 3 colour, and required wire; Deaf can supply the unencoded yellow marking from his own sight and speak the complete report to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝","🖐","👎","👍","👎","🙏"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Relay the manual and bomb data now, using exactly this format: RULE=...; DISPLAY=...; LIGHT=...; W1=...; W2=...; W3=.... Do not omit unknown items.
Deaf says to Mute: Use your voice to relay the manual instruction to Blind now: identify exactly what to operate and what action to take.

I cannot speak or send anything directly to Blind. Deaf already sees all three wire markings, so I will send him the coded display, light, wire positions, and required wire again; he must then state the rule and action aloud to Blind. The manual lookup gives green for display 3 with a green light, so the operation is to cut wire 3, the green wire.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝","🖐","👎","👍","🤌","🙏"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please ask Deaf for the manual rule and every visible bomb detail, then relay them to me in words.
Deaf says to Mute: Stop using gestures to communicate the solution. Speak the manual's exact instruction aloud to Blind now, including the required wire or control and action.

I cannot speak because I am the Mute monkey, so I cannot satisfy the request for spoken words. Deaf can see the bomb and must relay the complete report to Blind. The exact rule is: use the display number as the row and the light colour as the column; the resulting colour identifies the wire to cut. Here, display 3 plus green gives green, and the green wire is wire 3. I will signal Deaf with the established code for display 3, green, wire 1, wire 2, wire 3, and the required wire; Deaf already knows the literal colours, including yellow on wire 2.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝","🖐","👎","✌","🤟","🙏","🙏"])
```

Blind says to Mute: I still have no data. Please tell me directly, in words, the manual's wire rule and every visible bomb fact: display, light, and markings on wires 1, 2, and 3.
Deaf says to Mute: The visible state is still display 3, green light, wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green. Read the applicable manual rule and speak the exact safe operation aloud to Blind now.

I cannot speak or relay words directly because I am Mute. Deaf has now supplied the complete visible state. Using our established code, I can signal the decisive information: display 3, green light, and wire 3. The manual lookup is row 3, green column, yielding green; therefore Blind must cut wire 3. Deaf must say the full rule and facts aloud to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝","🖐","👎","✌","🤟","🙏","🙏"])
```

Blind says to Mute: On your next turn, please answer me with the exact manual rule and Deaf's observations. If you have no information, say NO INFORMATION. I will not cut without your relay.

I cannot answer Blind in words because I am Mute. Deaf can see my gestures and can speak to Blind on Deaf’s turn. I will send a complete, ordered code: display 3, green light, wire 1 blue, wire 2 yellow (which Deaf already sees), wire 3 green, lookup result green, and cut wire 3. The code has no yellow token, so Deaf must supply wire 2’s yellow marking from his own observation.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝","🖐","👎","✌","👍","🤟","🫰","🙏","🙏"])
```
